principles.title: I build it from the parts.
principles.text: Even when a library would do it. Once, so I know what is actually happening underneath.

principles.title: I build the broken version first.
principles.text: Then attack it, fix it, and run the same attack again to prove the fix holds.

principles.title: I test on the mess.
principles.text: Real phones, imperfect photos, bad network. The demo machine proves nothing.

experience.headline: A path, not a checklist.
experience.intro: Each step made the next question a little more ambitious, and a little closer to the physical world.

moments.title: Learned to make applications hold together.
moments.detail: At IUT Nantes, full-stack projects taught me the full path from an idea and a data model to something another person can actually use.

moments.title: Pointed computer vision at fiber-optic defects.
moments.detail: At FPT Telecom, accuracy was only one part of the job. Latency, messy images, documentation, and leaving a maintainable pipeline behind mattered too.

moments.title: Helped turn an NFC tag into a shipped product.
moments.detail: Waiki was the first time I led a team from a blank page to both app stores. It taught me that background reliability and team clarity are product features.

moments.title: Started breaking systems to understand them.
moments.detail: CTFs pulled me into cryptography, forensics, and OSINT. GardeFou brought that mindset to AI: build the vulnerable thing, attack it, then prove the defense works.

moments.title: Studying AI, while keeping one foot outside the model.
moments.detail: I’m at INSA Rennes, building backend tools for an accessibility association and looking for a summer 2027 internship where software meets a hard, real problem.

projects.heading: A few things I’ve built.
projects.outro: There are more experiments, useful tools, and ideas that got slightly out of hand.

01.question: What if self-control had a physical shape?
01.note: I led three students from a stubborn idea to a product people now carry in their pockets.
01.result: Live on iOS + Android · 1,425+ units sold

09.question: Could a document quietly hijack an AI?
09.note: Reading about prompt injection felt too comfortable, so I built a vulnerable assistant and attacked it myself.

10.question: What is a neural network hiding from me?
10.note: I built the DQN training loop in Rust and watched the agent slowly teach itself to survive.

03.question: Can a model cope with the mess outside a lab?
03.note: I compared vision models on imperfect plant photos to find the point where a benchmark becomes genuinely useful.

hobbies.body: Photography makes me slow down and notice geometry, light, and the one detail that changes the frame. It is the opposite of debugging, and somehow the same skill.
hobbies.boulderingText: A problem you solve with your whole body. Fall, adjust one move, try again.
hobbies.escapeText: Pattern recognition, questionable theories, and a timer making every idea louder.
